text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government discusses guidelines for private sector investment in setting up airports. Government to redistribute the population over 61 million acres (20 hectares) in the new and old valleys.

- Amid a positive atmosphere and support from most members of the Israeli government: Palestinians and Israelis make progress and there will be a meeting between (Palestinian President) Arafat and (Israeli prime minister) Netanyhau today.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says the Damascus Declaration meeting will have an open agenda.
- Local Government Minister Mahmoud Sherif says investment in Egypt's governorates totalled 78.2 billion pounds ($23 billion) during 1996.
- Youssef Boutros-Ghali, minister of state for economic cooperation, forecasts investments worth $5 billion will flow into Egypt next year.
- There will be an agreement on Hebron very soon. U.S. Mideast envoy Dennis Ross leaves Israel and will return next Monday to put the final touches.
- Ministers of the Damascus Declaration countries will meet in Cairo day after tomorrow.
- Catholic patriarch in his Christmas speech: The world has lauded President Mubarak's achievements.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid says state sold 25 million shares in 27 companies during 1996.
- Hebron agreement to be signed in a week's time. Palestinian sources say the issues of Martyr's Street and hot pursuit have been solved.
- Damascus Declaration states to discuss Jewish settlements.
- Electricity and Energy Minister Maher Abaza says government to adjust the prices of electricity to suit the consumer.
- Government to grant industrial projects set up in the new industrial zones a 60 percent tax exemption.
